items.title: Loren Schoenberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: I went down to meet him because Len had met him at the urologist’s office, and started to pitch a program to him... this program went on for several years... we must have done 150 concerts or something like that.

ctx.x: Yeah, yeah. Well the way it happened was there was a man named Donald Rubin who made a lot of money in health insurance. And he had more money than he knew what to do with. And he was nuts about, he was dedicated to Himalayan and culture and spirituality. So he built this vanity museum down on 18th Street I believe it is, off of Seventh Avenue, and he hired all the right people and got a brilliant programmer or a brilliant designer, and his vanity project wound up becoming one of the hippest, smartest, most…
